def:cs-gram-determinant-ratio:
Definition Chern--Simons Gram-determinant ratio \kappa. Let G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}} and G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} be the 2 \times 2 Gram matrices of the classical and the q-deformed Chern--Simons pairing on the rank-2 sublattice spanned by the force carriers T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} on Bring's surface (Chern--Simons descent correction), both written in one common basis, with \det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} \neq 0. The Gram-determinant ratio is

  \kappa \;:=\; \frac{\det G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}}}{\det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}}}.

A change of basis B with \det B \neq 0 sends each Gram matrix G to B^{\top} G B and multiplies each determinant by (\det B)^2, so \kappa does not depend on the basis chosen.

Conjecture Gram-determinant ratio \kappa as a Plancherel-weighted character product. Working over R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}], let \beta_s = T_{2,9}, \beta_w = T_{3,5}. Each admits a Wedderburn decomposition into central idempotents of the ambient Hecke algebra H_n(R, q):

  \beta_\bullet \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n}
    c_\lambda^{(\bullet)}\; e_\lambda,
  \qquad
  c_\lambda^{(\bullet)} \;=\; \chi_\lambda(\beta_\bullet) \in R.

Then the Gram-determinant ratio \kappa = \det G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}} / \det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} appearing in the Chern-Simons descent (CS coupling) is given by a Plancherel-weighted character product of the form

  \boxed{\;
  \kappa \;=\;
  \prod_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n}
    \left[
      \frac{\dim V_\lambda}{\dim_q V_\lambda}
      \cdot
      \frac{[n]_q!}{n!}
    \right]^{c_\lambda^{(s)}\, c_\lambda^{(w)}}
  \,\in\, R.
  \;}

The displayed product is not yet a well-defined element of R, and making it one is part of the conjecture. Two points are open: T_{2,9} is the closure of a braid on 2 strands and T_{3,5} of a braid on 3, so the two character families live on different Hecke algebras and the product over \lambda \vdash n needs a common n; and the exponents c_\lambda^{(s)} c_\lambda^{(w)} lie in R, not in \mathbb{Z}, so the powers are not defined in R.
